newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Arnotts product recall in NSW, QLD.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Arnotts product recall in NSW, QLD.

text.p: Australia's largest biscuit maker Arnotts Ltd had asked the major retailing chains to remove its entire product range from their shelves in the states of Queensland and New South Wales, the Australian Supermarket Institute said on Friday.
"Our member companies are beginning to take them off the shelves this morning," Institute Associate Director Ken Henrick told Reuters.
The Institutes membes include Woolworths Ltd, Coles Myer Ltd, Franklins, Davids Ltd and Foodland Associated Ltd.

"We were told about it yesterday and we understood there would be an announcement early afternoon today, but the Courier Mail (newspaper) has broken the embargo today and our member companies are going ahead and removing the entire range of Arnotts products," Henrick said. The products were likely to be removed from shelves by midday on Friday.
It was not clear how long the recall would last, he said.
Henrick said he could not say how much the product range being recalled was worth, except to say that Arnotts had a dominant position in the market.
"The recall is applying only to New South Wales and Queensland," he said.
"The perpetrator seems to be Queensland based and it looks as though that's where the threat is coming from."
Arnotts is 69.91 percent owned by Campbell Soup Co.
Queensland police said late on Thursday that an extortionist had threatened to plant the poisoned biscuits unless police involved in a murder case underwent a lie detector test.

Queensland police superintendent Ron Pickering told a news conference that an extortion letter and packages containing poisoned biscuits were received by a leading food company in the states of New South Wales and Queensland on February 3.
Police later confirmed the company was Arnotts.
Arnotts has not made any formal comment yet, but has requested a trading halt on their shares.
Arnotts' shares closed up five cents at A$8.75 on Thursday.
